root.title: Keep Orbit test gates out of caller databases
root.description:
Source: https://linear.app/nckrtl/issue/ORB-247/keep-orbit-test-gates-out-of-caller-databases
Package: orbit-orb-247-test-database-safety, revision 1; reviewed SHA-256 92c88b34b298372d2a3abf671388b5ceb2467e738fa16c653d6976af4e0b56f2.
Independent preparation review: /root/orb247_task_preparation_review, pass. Standing autonomous goal supplies execution authority; this is not a claim of a separate exact-revision human approval.
Repository: https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit
Inspected baseline: 317de2b630f7e8febdc3f2a25a664e10d14a6beb.
Flow: discovery; Incus not required. No topology allocation.
One executable child: guard-test-startup; no dependencies.

Objective: Orbit's supported local test entrypoints cannot migrate or mutate a caller's database, and unsafe effective test configuration fails before mutation without producing a successful candidate receipt.

Scope:

- In: Gateway test bootstrap, PHPUnit configurations, root/Gateway command integration, relevant Gateway tests and `apps/e2e/tests/Feature/**` or `apps/e2e/tests/Unit/**`, and local-check documentation.
- Out: Commander code and recovery, production database selection/migrations, harness runtime, discovery snapshots, DNS behavior, other product features, and new test-runner infrastructure.

Shared context:

- Follow Orbit's root and affected nested `AGENTS.md`; accepted ADR 0058 governs automated-only verification and ADR 0059 owns the candidate check and independent review. Both are accepted on the inspected main.
- The goal owner explicitly adopts this issue into Commander's task flow. Use this package instead of the legacy `.loop/plan.md` preparation contract. Documentation belongs in the accepted task commit. Do not remove unrelated legacy artifacts or alter other issues' flow.
- The external manager owns dispatch, review and merge. A fresh worker implements the single child and yields uncommitted changes; a separate retained reviewer requests corrections or approves and creates its clean commit. Final integrated review and the exact-candidate gate remain required.
- `apps/gateway/phpunit.xml` and `phpunit.guidance.xml` currently set memory SQLite defaults without forcing effective Laravel selection. `tests/Pest.php` applies `RefreshDatabase` to Feature tests, including serial guidance checks. `tests/TestCase.php` currently has no pre-mutation database guard.
- `apps/gateway/config/database.php` exposes `url => env('DB_URL')`. Laravel connection URL parsing can override the nominal database path. Inspect effective configuration, not only `getenv()` or XML text.
- A disposable diagnosis with the installed PHPUnit environment handler showed that `force="true"` can change `getenv('DB_DATABASE')` while Laravel still sees an inherited value in `$_SERVER`. A force-only XML change is not adequate evidence.
- Root `bin/review-check` invokes three commands per Composer project with inherited environment and writes `passed` from their exit codes plus candidate stability. `bin/test` and the Gateway Composer scripts are other supported paths. Avoid a new parallel implementation of the repository gate.
- The earlier ORB-242 gate overwrote an external Commander SQLite database despite reporting success. Reproduce only against task-owned temporary sentinel databases; never point an adversarial test at a real coordinator, project runtime, fleet database, or backup.
- The manager's caller-side isolation patch is separate defense. ORB-247 must work for direct local use without depending on Commander. Do not sanitize away adversarial variables in the test under examination and then claim Orbit protected them.
root.acceptance_criteria:
Feature acceptance (same order as Linear):

- F1: root candidate checks, Gateway Composer checks, and direct Gateway Pest never select the caller's database through inherited `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_URL`, or conflicting PHP environment/server sources. Sentinel schema, records and bytes remain unchanged.
- F2: unsafe effective connections, including unsafe cached Laravel configuration, fail nonzero before migrations or other database mutations.
- F3: serial guidance and parallel TIA still execute against supported disposable test databases; deliberately allocated test fixtures remain usable.
- F4: a safety refusal fails the candidate gate and cannot yield a successful receipt.
- F5: non-test Gateway database behavior is unchanged; contributor documentation explains safe configuration and recovery from refusal.

Final verification:

- All five feature criteria require child evidence mapped to exact subprocess scenarios, commands, exit status, and retained output where useful. File-hash assertions must accompany meaningful sentinel schema/record assertions.
- Run affected TIA tests and changed-project quality checks in `apps/gateway` and `apps/e2e`; run root `composer docs-lint` for documentation. New tests are to be added by the child, not currently passing acceptance evidence.
- After the reviewer creates the clean commit, Commander runs root `composer check` under its reviewed isolated subprocess boundary. Preserve the exact candidate and repository-produced receipt. The independent final reviewer inspects that receipt and the five acceptance outcomes; do not rerun the full gate solely for approval.
- No real-browser check is needed: this is test/bootstrap and contributor guidance only, with no user-visible UI change. No Incus fixture is required by these acceptance criteria.

children.title: Guard Gateway test database selection
children.description:
Objective: Supported Orbit test entrypoints protect caller databases at the test bootstrap boundary while continuing to run correctly with disposable test resources.

Scope:

- In: the root's bounded Gateway/test-command surfaces, their behavioral regression coverage, and `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md` local-check guidance.
- Out: the root exclusions. No unrelated guidance rewrite, dependency upgrade, product migration, or Incus provisioning repair.

Context:

- Consume the root's incident evidence and verified code references. One task is intentional: guard, effective-configuration regression tests, entrypoint propagation checks and documentation establish one atomic invariant and can ship as one coherent commit.
- Existing test references: Gateway `tests/Feature/Configuration/BoostGuidanceTest.php`, `tests/Unit/Configuration/BoostConfigurationTest.php`; E2E `tests/Feature/Configuration/ComposerConfigurationTest.php` and `AgentRoleContractTest.php`. Add behavioral fixtures beside suitable siblings; do not merely assert expected source strings.
- Relevant runtime/tooling references: Gateway `tests/TestCase.php`, `tests/Pest.php`, both PHPUnit files, `config/database.php`, `composer.json`; root `bin/review-check`, `bin/test`, and `composer.json`. Read installed Laravel/PHPUnit/Pest implementations or version-specific docs for actual bootstrap ordering and parallel database behavior.
- Keep default candidate-gate behavior, TIA policy, five-project separation and non-test Gateway configuration. Prefer a narrow PHP test bootstrap/guard and existing scripts over general orchestration changes.

Verification:

- V1: T1–T3/T5; `apps/gateway`; add isolated bootstrap/subprocess regression tests and run `composer test:affected`; expect all affected scenarios passing. New coverage is task output, not pre-existing evidence.
- V2: T1/T4; `apps/e2e`; add disposable gate/entrypoint regression fixtures under allowed test directories and run `composer test:affected`; expect proper refusal propagation and no successful failed-gate receipt. Keep the E2E application database-free; temporary sentinel SQLite files belong to subprocess fixtures, not E2E application state.
- V3: T1–T5; each changed Composer project; `composer check`; expect guidance, formatting, Rector and analysis checks passing under the existing command contract.
- V4: T5; repository root; `composer docs-lint`; expect updated contributor guidance to pass.
- V5: all F criteria; final clean accepted candidate; root `composer check` and independent review as defined above.

Outputs:

- Reviewable uncommitted implementation, regression tests and scoped documentation; the implementer does not commit.
- Acceptance-mapped evidence, including safe sentinel allocation and preservation, exact child entrypoints, observed failure/success exits and any unrun checks. Do not include secrets.
- One reviewer-created commit after pass, then final gate and independent integrated review before root completion or merge.

issue.title: Keep Orbit test gates out of caller databases
issue.description:
Orbit's local test commands keep caller databases unchanged, including when another Laravel application launches the candidate gate. At candidate `2073e852bdc121f7876bf42be28f4b41d899d7a0`, Commander's inherited SQLite configuration reached Gateway guidance tests and `RefreshDatabase` replaced its task database with Gateway tables; the gate nevertheless reported success.

## Scope

* In: Gateway test bootstrap and both PHPUnit configurations, root and Gateway test-command integration, and focused regression tests for effective database selection.
* In: candidate-gate regression tests under `apps/e2e/tests/Feature/` or `apps/e2e/tests/Unit/`, and maintained local-check guidance.
* Out: Commander subprocess isolation and ledger recovery, production database configuration and migrations, Incus harness behavior, snapshot provisioning, and DNS behavior.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Supported root candidate checks, Gateway Composer checks, and direct Gateway Pest runs cannot use an inherited caller database through `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_URL`, or conflicting PHP environment/server values. Proof: disposable subprocess regression tests exercise these entrypoints with a sentinel SQLite database and assert its schema, records, and file hash remain unchanged.
- [ ] An unsafe effective database connection is refused before migration or other database mutation, including when cached Laravel configuration selects it. Proof: a disposable cached-configuration fixture points at the sentinel database and the test observes nonzero refusal before any schema or data change.
- [ ] Serial guidance checks and parallel TIA test execution retain their supported disposable database behavior after isolation. Proof: Gateway TIA tests and subprocess fixtures exercise both configurations and the parallel test path, preserving deliberately allocated test fixtures.
- [ ] A database-safety refusal fails the candidate gate and cannot produce a successful receipt. Proof: candidate-gate regression tests inspect the failing command result and the resulting receipt.
- [ ] Normal non-test Gateway database configuration remains unchanged, and contributor guidance explains safe test configuration and refusal recovery. Proof: configuration regression tests compare a non-test fixture's effective connection, and `composer docs-lint` checks the updated local-check guidance.
